title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
tldr: Predicting masked video in latent space at internet scale, then bolting on 62 hours of unlabeled robot video, is enough to plan real pick-and-place zero-shot.

problem.task: Action-free video representation learning, then action-conditioned latent prediction for planning.

inputs.name: video
inputs.chars: 64 frames at 256px for the encoder; robot arm views for the AC head.

inputs.name: goal image
inputs.chars: Planning only: a photo of the desired end state.

outputs.name: latent state
outputs.chars: Patch-level embeddings used for probing, VQA, anticipation.

outputs.name: end-effector action
outputs.chars: Planning only: chosen by CEM over rolled-out latents, replanned each step.

training.supervision: Self-supervised masked latent prediction — no labels, no actions. A second stage adds action conditioning from unlabeled robot video.
training.note: Stage 1 sees 1M+ hours of internet video and never sees an action. Stage 2 sees <62 h of Droid video with actions and freezes the encoder.

method.intuition: Predicting pixels wastes capacity on detail that does not matter for acting, so predict the representation instead and let the encoder decide what is worth keeping.

experiments.headline: 77.3 top-1 on SSv2 and 39.7 recall@5 on EK100 anticipation. Picks and places on Franka arms in two labs it never saw data from.

why: The clearest single statement that a world model can be learned by observation alone and still reach into the physical world.

title: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
tldr: Latent actions can be recovered from unlabeled internet video, which turns any video corpus into a controllable environment.

problem.task: Unsupervised learning of an action-controllable video world model from action-free video.

inputs.name: prompt frame
inputs.chars: Text-to-image output, a photograph, or a hand sketch.

inputs.name: latent action
inputs.chars: One of 8 discrete codes, chosen by the user per frame.

outputs.name: next frame
outputs.chars: Autoregressive, frame by frame — the environment is the rollout.

training.supervision: Fully unsupervised on 200k+ hours of 2D platformer video. No action labels anywhere.
training.note: The latent action model is trained inside the reconstruction objective, so the action vocabulary is discovered, not given.

method.intuition: If a model must explain the next frame from the previous frame plus a tiny bottleneck, the bottleneck is forced to become the action.
components: latent action model with an 8-code VQ bottleneck

baselines: action-conditioned world models with ground-truth actions
experiments.headline: Frame-level controllability from unlabeled video. The learned latent actions transfer well enough to imitate behaviour from unseen videos.

why: Reframes the data problem in physical AI: the bottleneck was never video, it was action labels, and this shows they can be inferred.

title: Cosmos World Foundation Model Platform for Physical AI
tldr: Ships the whole stack — curation pipeline, tokenizers, pretrained world models — on the premise that a physical AI system needs a digital twin of the world before it touches the real one.

problem.task: General-purpose video world model, meant to be post-trained into a task-specific one.

inputs.name: conditioning
inputs.chars: Past frames, or a single image, or text.

inputs.name: control
inputs.chars: Optional, added in post-training: robot actions, camera pose, or trajectory.

outputs.name: future video
outputs.chars: Continuation that is meant to obey physics rather than only look good.

training.supervision: Next-token / denoising on a curated 20M-hour-scale video corpus. Post-training adds control signals.
training.note: The curation pipeline is the part most likely to be reused — deduplication, shot detection, quality and motion filtering.

method.intuition: Treat the world model as a foundation model: pretrain broadly, then post-train into driving, manipulation, or humanoid variants rather than training each from scratch.

experiments.headline: Open-weight world models with post-training recipes for camera control, robotic manipulation and autonomous driving.

why: The paper that made "physical AI" a named product category, and the reference for what a world-model pipeline contains end to end.

title: Back to the Features: DINO as a Foundation for Video World Models
tldr: Freeze DINOv2 and train only a future predictor on top: a strong video world model without learning a visual encoder at all.

problem.task: Predict future frames in a frozen self-supervised feature space; optionally condition on actions and plan.

inputs.name: past features
inputs.chars: DINOv2 patch tokens, encoder frozen.

inputs.name: action
inputs.chars: Only in the fine-tuned action-conditioned variant.

outputs.name: future features
outputs.chars: Decoded with light heads into segmentation or depth for evaluation.

training.supervision: Future-feature regression on large-scale uncurated video. Encoder never updated.
training.note: Action conditioning is a small fine-tune on observation-action trajectories.

method.intuition: A good frozen encoder already supplies a space worth predicting in, which leaves the dynamics as the hard part of a world model.

experiments.headline: Beats prior video-prediction models on forecasting benchmarks and plans by simulating candidate trajectories in latent space.

why: Isolates the variable: how much of a world model's power comes from the representation versus the dynamics head.

title: Causal-JEPA: Learning World Models through Object-Level Latent Masking
tldr: Mask whole objects instead of image patches, and the model has to learn how objects affect each other rather than inpainting texture.

problem.task: Object-centric latent world modeling, evaluated by counterfactual VQA and by planning efficiency.

inputs.name: frame
inputs.chars: Scenes with several interacting objects.

inputs.name: object slots
inputs.chars: K object-level latents, a small fraction of the patch-token count.

outputs.name: predicted object latents
outputs.chars: Masked objects inferred from the surrounding objects.

training.supervision: Self-supervised: predict masked object latents from unmasked ones.
training.note: Masking at object granularity is what creates the counterfactual query — the model cannot fall back on local texture.

method.intuition: Object-centric slots alone do not force a model to learn interaction. Hiding a whole object and demanding its state from context does.

baselines: patch-masked JEPA with the same architecture
experiments.headline: About +20 points absolute on counterfactual reasoning over the same architecture without object-level masking, and comparable planning using 1% of the latent features.

why: The object-centric argument stated at its sharpest: the granularity of the masking objective is the inductive bias.

title: Object Concepts Emerge from Motion
tldr: Motion boundaries are free instance labels: cluster optical flow into pseudo-masks and train a contrastive encoder that learns objecthood without a single annotation.

problem.task: Unsupervised object-centric representation learning from raw video.

inputs.name: image
inputs.chars: Single frame at test time; no flow needed.

outputs.name: dense features
outputs.chars: Instance-aware features probed for depth, 3D detection, occupancy.

training.supervision: None. Pseudo instance masks come from off-the-shelf optical flow plus clustering.
training.note: No camera calibration required, which is what makes it scale to unstructured video.

method.intuition: Infants learn objecthood by watching things move together. Motion boundaries are the same signal, and they are already computable.

experiments.headline: Outperforms supervised and self-supervised baselines on all three probes and transfers to unseen scenes.

why: Argues that vision foundation models skip a level of abstraction — the instance — and that motion is the cheapest way to recover it.

title: PointWorld: Scaling 3D World Models for In-The-Wild Robotic Manipulation
tldr: Put state and action in the same 3D space as point flow, and one world model serves a Franka and a bimanual humanoid without an embodiment-specific action head.

problem.task: Action-conditioned 3D forecasting: given RGB-D and a command, predict where every point goes.

inputs.name: RGB-D
inputs.chars: One or a few views; open-world scenes, not a fixed rig.

inputs.name: action sequence
inputs.chars: Low-level robot commands, re-expressed as 3D point flow of the robot geometry.

outputs.name: 3D point flow
outputs.chars: Per-pixel displacement in 3D, at 0.1 s inference, consumed by MPC.

training.supervision: Supervised point-flow forecasting on ~2M real and simulated manipulation trajectories (~500 h).
training.note: Because actions are geometry, a single-arm Franka and a bimanual humanoid share one action space.

method.intuition: Embodiment-specific action spaces are what stop world models from pooling data. Express the action as motion of the robot's own geometry and the barrier disappears.

experiments.headline: One pre-trained checkpoint drives a real Franka through rigid-body manipulation at real-time (0.1 s) inference, with an ablation study over backbones, action representations and data mixtures.

why: The cleanest counter-argument to pixel-space world models: geometry is the shared coordinate system across embodiments.

title: Whole-Body Conditioned Egocentric Video Prediction
tldr: Condition egocentric video prediction on 3D body pose instead of a robot action vector, and the world model's action space becomes the human body.

problem.task: Given past egocentric video and a whole-body action, predict the next egocentric frames.

inputs.name: past video
inputs.chars: First-person view from a head-mounted camera.

inputs.name: body action
inputs.chars: Relative 3D joint positions, structured by the kinematic hierarchy — not a 7-DoF gripper vector.

training.supervision: Paired egocentric video and body pose from Nymeria.
training.note: Pose comes from real motion capture in the wild, which is what makes the action space physically meaningful.

method.intuition: For a human-embodied world model the action is the body, so structure the conditioning by the joint hierarchy rather than flattening it.
components: graded evaluation protocol by horizon and difficulty

metrics: perceptual and pixel similarity at multiple horizons
experiments.headline: A hierarchical evaluation protocol of increasingly hard prediction and control tasks. Body-conditioned prediction holds up where unconditioned prediction drifts.

why: The human-embodiment counterpart to robot world models: same machinery, but the action space is a person.

title: Genie Envisioner: A Unified World Foundation Platform for Robotic Manipulation
tldr: One video-generative latent serves three roles at once: the policy, the simulator it is evaluated in, and the benchmark that scores it.

problem.task: Instruction-conditioned video world model, with an action decoder and a neural simulator built on the same latent.

inputs.name: observation
inputs.chars: Multi-view robot camera streams.

inputs.name: instruction
inputs.chars: Free-form task command.

outputs.name: action trajectory
outputs.chars: GE-Act — a light flow-matching decoder off the same latent.

training.supervision: Large-scale instruction-conditioned robot video, then a small decoder fit for each embodiment.
training.note: GE-Sim reuses the same model action-conditioned, so evaluation rollouts and policy rollouts share one dynamics model.

method.intuition: If a video model already contains the dynamics, then policy, simulator and evaluator are three read-outs of one latent, not three systems.

experiments.headline: One platform covering policy learning, closed-loop simulation and benchmarking, transferring across embodiments with a lightweight decoder.

why: Makes the loop literal: the same model predicts the world, acts in it, and grades the result.

title: WorldPrediction: A Benchmark for High-level World Modeling and Long-horizon Procedural Planning
tldr: Tests world models at the level of semantic actions rather than pixels, and blocks the usual shortcut by giving distractors that are the same action filmed elsewhere.

problem.task: Discriminate the correct action (WM) or the correctly ordered action sequence (PP) between an initial and a final world state.

inputs.name: initial state
inputs.chars: Visual observation of the world before.

inputs.name: final state
inputs.chars: Visual observation of the world after.

inputs.name: candidates
inputs.chars: Includes action equivalents — the same action in a different context — so background continuity cannot be exploited.

outputs.name: choice
outputs.chars: Discriminative, so generative and non-generative models can be compared on one scale.

training.note: Grounded in a partially observable semi-MDP formalism, which is what lets the two subtasks share a scale.

method.intuition: Most world-model benchmarks reward low-level pixel continuity. Abstract actions are where planning actually lives, so score those instead.

experiments.headline: A discriminative setup that puts generative world models and planners on the same axis at semantic rather than pixel granularity.

why: Names the gap between low-level world modeling and the temporal abstraction that procedural tasks actually need.

title: DINOv2: Learning Robust Visual Features without Supervision
tldr: Curated data plus scale makes self-supervised features that work off the shelf, which is why half the world models on this list start by freezing it.

problem.task: General-purpose visual features usable without fine-tuning.

inputs.name: image
inputs.chars: Any natural image.

outputs.name: features
outputs.chars: Patch tokens carry dense correspondence, which is why they work for geometry probes.

training.supervision: Self-distillation with no labels, on an automatically curated 142M-image set (LVD-142M).
training.note: The curation pipeline — retrieval from an uncurated pool against a curated seed — is as much the contribution as the objective.

method.intuition: Self-supervision was not the bottleneck. Data curation was.

experiments.headline: Surpasses OpenCLIP on most image- and pixel-level benchmarks without any fine-tuning.

why: Sits under a large fraction of this list. Background reading rather than a physical AI paper in itself.

title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
tldr: Streaming memory turns promptable segmentation into object tracking, which is the cheapest way to get object identity across time.

problem.task: Promptable visual segmentation in video: a click on one frame yields a mask on every frame.

inputs.name: video
inputs.chars: Processed frame by frame with a memory bank, so it runs online.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.chars: On any frame, at any time; corrections can be added mid-stream.

outputs.name: masklet
outputs.chars: One object tracked through occlusion and re-appearance.

training.supervision: Supervised on SA-V, itself built by a model-in-the-loop data engine with human annotators.
training.note: The data engine is the mechanism: better model → faster annotation → more data → better model.

method.intuition: Video segmentation is image segmentation plus memory, and the memory can be a plain streaming bank rather than a specialised tracker.

experiments.headline: Better video accuracy with 3× fewer interactions, and 6× faster than SAM on images.

why: The practical answer to "how do I get object identity over time" that most object-centric pipelines on this list quietly depend on.
